2_Introduction: By interlinking experimental conditions with device architecture, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, affirming a PCE of 23.4914%, FF of 82.0602%, Voc of 1.1271 V, and Jsc of 25.398 mA/cm². 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solutions were prepared with the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. For the perovskite film fabrication, the substrate was spun at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 160 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 10 s before the end of the program. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture exhibiting an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide vacancy formation energy—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization under the specified spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s nucleation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s growth), where the precisely timed antisolvent quenching at 10 s prior to spin termination induces rapid supersaturation, favoring homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and thereby minimizing pinhole formation and interfacial voids; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent evaporation while promoting grain coalescence and strain relaxation, as corroborated by XRD showing full suppression of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of high crystallinity, low microstrain, and phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ dominance—while optical and PL mapping reveal uniform film coverage (>99.2% continuity), negligible grayscale intensity fluctuations (<3% RSD), and spatially homogeneous PL intensity with a monoexponential decay (τₐᵥₑ = 1.24 μs), collectively evidencing suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways across the entire active area and confirming that the crystallization dynamics successfully mitigate both bulk trap states (e.g., I⁻ vacancies, Pb²⁺ antisites) and interfacial defects at the perovskite/charge transport layer boundary; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition—where FA⁺ enhances lattice stability and octahedral connectivity, MA⁺ improves crystallization kinetics without inducing phase segregation, and Cs⁺ rigidifies the lattice and suppresses ion migration—synergistically stabilizes the perovskite against thermal- and electric-field-induced degradation while maintaining favorable band alignment for hole extraction, resulting in VOC of 1.1271 V, JSC of 25.398 mA/cm², FF of 82.0602%, and PCE of 23.4914%.
